# s390 — The post-merge hook says when slicer is missing, and a test runs its install command

**Findings:** s384 relay report 2026-10-22, later notes 1 and 3: when slicer is not on PATH the hook prints only "run slicer check", and no test runs the printed install command · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** installing the hook for the person, the roadmap-only detection, and a change to the merge driver.

## Why

`_post_merge_hook` in `src/slicer/cli.py` captures `slicer check --json` and, for any status other than the roadmap-only case, prints "merge check needs attention; run slicer check." When `slicer` is not on PATH the shell status is 127, so the person is told to run a command that is the very thing missing. The s384 tests assert the install command's text but none runs it, so a quoting mistake in the `git rev-parse --git-path` form would pass the suite.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`_post_merge_hook`).
- `tests/test_cli.py`, next to the s384 post-merge hook tests.
- `docs/commands.md` (the `setup-git` row) and `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed, if the hook text is described there.

## Failing tests

- `test_PostMergeHook_SlicerNotOnPath_NamesTheMissingCommand`: run the printed hook with a PATH that has no `slicer`; it prints a line that says slicer was not found, exits 0 and renders nothing.
- `test_SetupGit_HookInstall_CommandInstallsExecutableHook`: in a fixture git repo, run the printed install command through `sh`; `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/post-merge` names an executable file with the hook text, and a `core.hooksPath` setting is honoured.

## Implement

1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. In the hook, test for status 127 before the other cases and print a line that says slicer was not found on PATH. The status stays 0.
3. Update the docs and CHANGELOG if they describe the hook text.
4. Mutation-check each new test.

## Check

- `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.
